scope: KQP-owned RANGE MIN/MAX runtime, compiler and type annotation integration; finite lower bound and finite or UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING upper bound. Also reviewed the matching small ROWS suffix eligibility extension.

evidence: mkql_computation_node_holders.h:5 imports the computation-node implementation; TMutableComputationNode inherits the mutables constructor with default Any representation at mkql_computation_node_impl.h:220-250.
The collector factory type is obtained from public CreateFactory, with no reference to its private precomputed type. Its signature matches mkql_queue.cpp:613-638.

Compiler callback captures TKqpBuildContext separately from its TMkqlBuildContext argument; builder returns the unchanged input stream type. Existing runtime PEERDIR dependencies provide the public collector deserializer.

BuildChainOutputs uses BuildResultFromAccumulator, whose optionality follows Window.GetIUType; BuildOutputRowType uses the same declarations. Mapping admission strips at most one optional and requires the same data annotation, including Decimal parameters.

The runtime repeats exact MiniKQL type equality and shared scalar-slot admission. Float, Double, timezone and composite aggregate inputs remain excluded. Present primitive optional values use the same unboxed representation; empty values are skipped and only optional outputs may be empty.
The existing cumulative-chain MIN/MAX placeholders remain linear work; the custom node overwrites fresh result fields while preserving original argument and sort fields.

CreateFactory owns precomputed bounds in its closure, and collector references point into that node-owned closure. The node owner remains alive under the same computation graph lifetime contract used by WinFramesCollector/TAggregateWindowValue in mkql_queue.cpp:440-535.
Buffer and Bounds members precede Collector; constructor does not consume input. Candidate values and copied output members own their references, so later buffer eviction cannot invalidate outputs.

Fetched increments only after successful input Fetch and successful reservation, matching the collector consumer successful-row count. A Yield can occur after several buffered fetches; the collector retains them and retries without advancing the current output row.

The collector removes a contiguous prefix only; absolute base is Fetched minus Buffer.Size. Public frame indices are rebased by the collector, and generation changes caused by PushBack/PopFront are owned by its Next cycle. Reserve preserves logical order without mutating generation.
All candidate indices are absolute; expiry precedes additions. SeenEnd covers both forward frame edges, including empty gaps. No range view or borrowed row pointer is retained across Next.

Candidate deques and their outer vector use TMKQLAllocator. The public buffer uses std::vector, so the wrapper charges new storage before Reserve and releases the old charge afterward, accounting for peak overlapping allocations.

OffloadAlloc limit/callback exceptions precede its counter changes (aligned_page_pool.cpp:113-141), so a pre-reserve rejection needs no undo. A Reserve exception releases only the new charge; destruction clears the buffer and releases the old charge. No failed query is resumed after a reserve exception.

Finish cleans candidates, clears buffer storage and zeroes BufferBytes. Subsequent Fetch returns Finish before touching the cleared collector; destruction therefore cannot double-release the buffer charge.

Runtime accepts an infinite upper bound only in Following direction and still requires finite lower. Existing ShouldAddElement makes the public collector drain the partition once; the absolute right edge then remains fixed. Expiry continues against the finite moving lower edge.

For ROWS, the first nonempty frame scans its suffix once; subsequent rows have the same last ordinal and append nothing, using existing two-stack expiry. The existing current-row suffix special path is selected earlier and is unchanged.
KqpRangeMinMax is registered in the KQP base compute factory, compiler and type transformer, with runtime source in ya.make. No essentials file is changed.

MIN/MAX-only frames bypass the second collector. Mixed frames retain it, and final result assembly reads the custom MIN/MAX columns while existing aggregate paths use original input/cumulative columns.

limitations: Source inspection is not compiler, native, allocator-failure-injection or distributed-placement evidence.
Mixed frames retain a second buffer and extra lookahead; benchmark memory and latency separately from correctness.
The finite-lower window scope and admitted scalar value families do not close every possible Q01 frame/type.
The callable validates the internal emitted mapping contract; malformed hand-built callable combinations are not a supported query input path.
